binders: Universally quantify a real number c.

Under the assumption c>0, the first conjunct existentially quantifies a family λ: Fin 1 → R and a basis b of the real vector space Fin 1 → R, indexed by Fin 1; their choice may depend on c. It then universally quantifies p in Fin 1.
The second conjunct universally quantifies x,t₁,t₂ in R.
The third conjunct universally quantifies a function f: R → R and a real number d, corresponding to the implicit Lean binders profile and profile', followed by x,t in R.

Inside the third conjunct's derivative implication, existentially quantify real numbers qt and qx. These witnesses are local to the chosen c,f,d,x,t and derivative hypothesis; qx is quantified after qt. No uniform derivative functions are selected.
hypotheses: The second conjunct assumes t₁<t₂ for its chosen x,t₁,t₂.
The third conjunct assumes that f has derivative d at x−ct, that is, lim as h→0 with h≠0 of (f(x−ct+h)−f(x−ct))/h equals d.
conclusions: For A=[c], there exist λ: Fin 1 → R and a real basis b of Fin 1 → R such that A b(p)=λ(p)•b(p) for every p in Fin 1.
For every x,t₁,t₂ in R with t₁<t₂, one has x+ct₁<x+ct₂.

For every f: R → R, d in R, and x,t in R, if f has derivative d at x−ct, then, writing w(ξ,τ)=f(ξ−cτ), there exist qt,qx in R such that τ ↦ w(x,τ) has derivative qt at t, ξ ↦ w(ξ,t) has derivative qx at x, and qt+c qx=0.
Under the same derivative hypothesis in the third conjunct, w(x+ct,t)=f(x), equivalently f((x+ct)−ct)=f(x).
mathematical_definitions: Fin 1 is the singleton index set {0}; its real coordinate space consists of functions {0} → R.
A(i,j)=c for all i,j in Fin 1, so A is the one-by-one real matrix [c]. Matrix-vector multiplication is (Av)(i)=Σ_j A(i,j)v(j).
A real eigenbasis means a basis b of the full real coordinate space together with real scalars λ(p) satisfying A b(p)=λ(p)b(p). The scalar λ(p) scales each coordinate of b(p).
The moving-profile function is w(ξ,τ)=f(ξ−cτ), with its first argument serving as space and its second as time.

The pointwise differential predicate asserts existence of both ordinary partial derivatives separately at (x,t), and their equation w_t(x,t)+c w_x(x,t)=0. It does not define derivatives by a totalized derivative operator.
All derivative predicates use ordinary real differentiation on the full real line, with the usual absolute-value metric and real scalar multiplication.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive real number c, the following three assertions hold simultaneously. First, the one-by-one matrix [c] has a basis of real eigenvectors: there are λ: {0} → R and a basis b of R^{ {0} } such that [c]b(p)=λ(p)b(p) for every p in {0}. Second, for each real x, the function t ↦ x+ct is strictly increasing on R. Third, for every real-valued profile f on R, every real derivative value d, and every real point (x,t), if f has derivative d at x−ct, then the function w(ξ,τ)=f(ξ−cτ) has both partial derivatives at (x,t), those derivatives satisfy w_t(x,t)+c w_x(x,t)=0, and w(x+ct,t)=f(x).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem is conditional on c>0; it makes no assertion for c≤0.
The matrix dimension is fixed at 1. Although D006 is defined for arbitrary finite index types, the target does not assert a result for general matrices or systems.
The matrix index set is nonempty, so its eigenvector condition is not an empty-index universal statement. The basis requirement excludes choosing only zero vectors.

The eigenbasis predicate does not explicitly require positive eigenvalues, distinct eigenvalues, normalization, or orthogonality. For this particular matrix the eigenvalue necessarily equals c, but the target does not prescribe that witness explicitly.
The coordinates and times range over all of R; no nonnegative-time, bounded-space, boundary, or initial-domain restriction appears.
The profile is real-valued. The polymorphic definitions do not make the target a theorem about arbitrary vector-valued profiles.
Differentiability is assumed only at x−ct for each application of the third conjunct. No global differentiability, continuous derivatives, or joint differentiability is assumed or asserted.
Where f has no derivative at x−ct, the third implication supplies no conclusion. For a proposed d that is not its derivative, the implication is also vacuous.
The equality w(x+ct,t)=f(x) lies inside the derivative implication, even though its displayed formula is algebraically valid without that hypothesis.
The derivative witnesses are required only to be derivatives of the two slices and satisfy qt+c qx=0. The target does not explicitly state qt=−cd or qx=d.

The declaration concerns the explicitly constructed function w. It does not classify all solutions of the differential equation, assert uniqueness, or separately specify an initial or boundary value problem.
Strict increase of t ↦ x+ct and constancy of w along the displayed shifted evaluation are encoded explicitly; any further physical interpretation is not part of the proposition.
